updates.name: As a Metro by T-Mobile authorized dealer, I want to add a customer's own tablet as a second line on an order and see it charged at nothing, so that the customer pays only for the SIM and the service
updates.custom_requirements:
## What this test is about
When a customer comes into a Metro by T-Mobile store to start service, the store usually sells them the device as well. Some customers already own the device they want on the account - very often a tablet they bought elsewhere - and they only want service for it. The trade calls this BYOD, bring your own device; when the device is a tablet the store calls it BYOT. A tablet is almost never the customer's only line: it sits alongside a phone, so the rep sets up the phone line first and then adds the tablet to the same order. The rep's job on the tablet line is to tell the system the tablet belongs to the customer rather than to the store, so the tablet itself is never charged for. The customer pays for the SIM, the monthly plan, and tax on those - and nothing for the tablet. Getting that wrong is expensive in both directions: charge for the tablet and the customer is billed for something they walked in holding; fail to register it properly and the tablet is never activated on the network. This test walks the whole thing: a first line completed, then the customer's tablet added as the second line, right up to the order summary.

Words used in this test: an IMEI is the 15-digit serial number that identifies a phone or tablet; a device with two SIM slots has two IMEIs. A SIM number (also called ICCID) is the long number printed on a physical SIM card. An eSIM is a SIM built into the device, identified by its EID. BYOD (bring your own device) means the customer already owns the device; the screen calls a customer's own phone BYOP (bring your own phone) and a customer's own tablet simply Tablet. A plan code such as TAB30SD is the carrier's short name for a monthly plan. MRC means the monthly recurring charge.

## Related tickets
RTPL-2061 (BYOD epic), RTPL-2205 (device type selection and second-IMEI rules), RTPL-2077 (device registration form), RTPL-2574 (Tablet added to the picker), RTPL-2403 (the chosen device type must be kept)

## Preconditions
- The rep can sign in to RT Go on the QA site with the team's QA sign-in, and the Metro environment in the user menu (top right) is set to UAT3.
- A brand-new account is being created; the order has no lines on it yet.
- Customer credential capture on the customer tablet is switched off for this store, so the PIN and security questions are filled in on the till screen. The customer-facing signature tablet plays no part in this test.
- Two unused SIM numbers are to hand, one for each line, and two customer-owned devices the carrier has not yet registered: one phone and one tablet, each with two SIM slots.

## Test data
- **Customer's phone for the first line:** IMEI 350108847628507, second IMEI 350108849530495  _(verified: UAT3 2026-09-24, walked click by click on the screen (build 5.924.0); this pair is now registered and cannot be used again - take the next unused pair from the same block (see notes))_
- **Customer's tablet for the second line:** IMEI 350108847196786, second IMEI 350108841755116  _(verified: UAT3 2026-09-24, walked click by click on the screen (build 5.924.0); this pair is now registered and cannot be used again - take the next unused pair from the same block (see notes))_
- **SIM numbers:** 8901260000075259986F for the phone, 8901260000075259995F for the tablet; spare: 8901260000075260000F, 8901260000075260019F  _(verified: UAT3 2026-09-24, walked click by click on the screen (build 5.924.0); 8901260000075259968F was refused as already used)_
- **Customer details:** Alex Tester, 1234 NE 1st St, zip 33179, PIN 135790, any three security questions, a new email each run using letters and digits only  _(verified: UAT3 2026-09-24, walked click by click on the screen (build 5.924.0); an email with a plus sign was refused with the message subscriberEmailAddress field format error)_
- **Store:** EZLOGIC, dealer code 30247306; the station is the one you sign in on  _(verified: UAT3 2026-09-24, walked click by click on the screen (build 5.924.0); the header showed Station Omran for this run)_
- **Expected charges:** Tablet line: device $0.00, SIM card $11.00, plan TAB30SD $30.00 a month; order summary Total MRC $90.00, taxes and fees $10.70  _(verified: UAT3 2026-09-24, walked click by click on the screen (build 5.924.0), Miami (FL) number)_

## Automation Notes
- Both devices are used up by every run. Choosing a device type registers the device with the carrier, so the same phone or tablet will not show the device-type screen again. Take a new pair for each line every run from the RTGO Data workbook, tab UAT2_BYODBYOW, rows whose IMEI starts 350108 (they work on UAT3). Pairs not yet tried: 350108845671228 / 350108846697495, 350108849128084 / 350108843338754, 350108846539671 / 350108844710688, 350108841926717 / 350108848332034. Check each one reaches the Add BYOD device screen before relying on it.
- A device that was already registered on an earlier run behaves differently: on 24 September 2026 the tablet 350108843291805 skipped the device-type, second-IMEI and SIM screens and was given an eSIM automatically. If that happens, the device is used up - take the next pair.
- If several pairs in a row are refused or behave differently from these steps, contact the manual QA team to help get working data rather than staying blocked or hunting for data alone.
- Always switch the SIM step to IMEI 1 - PSIM. Continuing on the eSIM choice has stalled on an endless loading spinner in past runs.
- Do not hard-code plan codes or prices. They follow the market of the phone number. What must hold on the tablet line is that every plan offered is a tablet plan and no phone plan appears.
- Error messages appear at the top right of the screen and disappear after a few seconds. Read them at the moment they appear.
- An order left idle for 60 minutes is cancelled automatically. If later steps fail with a message about the order already being cancelled, start again rather than debugging the step.

updates.name: As a Metro by T-Mobile authorized dealer, I want a device whose IMEI fails the carrier's own check to be refused clearly, so that I am not left with an order I cannot finish or undo
updates.custom_requirements:
## What this test is about
An IMEI is the 15-digit serial number that identifies a phone or tablet, and it carries its own built-in check digit, so a mistyped or made-up number can be spotted as invalid without asking anyone. The store's own screen checks only that the number is 15 digits, so it accepts a number that is the right length but not a real IMEI. The carrier applies the stricter test at the moment the device is registered - one screen after the rep typed the number, once the rep has chosen what kind of device it is. This test covers what the rep sees at that point and whether the rep can get back to correct the number, because an order that can be neither finished nor corrected is the worst outcome at a busy counter.

Words used in this test: an IMEI is the 15-digit serial number that identifies a phone or tablet; a device with two SIM slots has two IMEIs. A SIM number (also called ICCID) is the long number printed on a physical SIM card. An eSIM is a SIM built into the device, identified by its EID. BYOD (bring your own device) means the customer already owns the device; the screen calls a customer's own phone BYOP (bring your own phone) and a customer's own tablet simply Tablet. A plan code such as TAB30SD is the carrier's short name for a monthly plan. MRC means the monthly recurring charge.

## Related tickets
RTPL-2076 (device validation prompts), RTPL-2205 (device registration)

## Preconditions
- The rep can sign in to RT Go on the QA site with the team's QA sign-in, and the Metro environment in the user menu (top right) is set to UAT3.
- A brand-new account is being created; the order has no lines on it yet.
- Customer credential capture on the customer tablet is switched off for this store, so the PIN and security questions are filled in on the till screen. The customer-facing signature tablet plays no part in this test.

## Test data
- **IMEI that fails the carrier's check:** 958127484993407  _(verified: UAT3 2026-09-24, walked click by click on the screen (build 5.924.0); the screen accepted it and offered registration, and the carrier refused it when Tablet was chosen. It is never used up, so it can be used on every run)_
- **Expected refusal:** Metro Proxy request failed: Entered IMEI is Invalid, Check Digit Validation Failed. (Error No: 210063043)  _(verified: UAT3 2026-09-24, walked click by click on the screen (build 5.924.0), read from the message at the top right of the screen)_
- **Customer details:** Alex Tester, 1234 NE 1st St, zip 33179, PIN 135790, any three security questions, a new email each run using letters and digits only  _(verified: UAT3 2026-09-24, walked click by click on the screen (build 5.924.0))_

## Automation Notes
- Read the refusal the moment it appears - it is a message at the top right that disappears after a few seconds. Assert the exact wording including the error number 210063043, and assert that the screen does not move on to SIM validation.
- The back arrow removes the line without asking the rep to confirm. If a later build adds a confirmation, update the last step to expect it.
- This IMEI is deliberately invalid, so it is never used up and can be used on every run.
